subject: Mode qualification and PoC charter — MedStream follow-up
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Ethan Clarke <ethan.clarke@medstream.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mode qualification and PoC charter — MedStream follow-up

Hi Ethan — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we can lock the PoC approach: 

Call recap (short):
- Primary use case: real-time discharge summary generation from streaming clinical notes (PHI).
- Key constraints: data residency (US-only), strict audit/KMS needs, and sustained burst traffic during end-of-day processing windows.
- Stakeholders you named: Ethan (ML/Product), Procurement (legal/contracting), and Ops (infra).

Mode qualification questions we need to resolve to scope the PoC:
1) Security/regulatory preference: you mentioned Private VPC as the long-term target. Is Private VPC required for the PoC, or would MedStream accept a Dedicated pool (isolated GPUs) for the trial while security completes the VPC onboarding?
2) Performance targets: please confirm P95 token-latency target and expected concurrent streams during peak (you mentioned ~120 concurrent).
3) Data flow: will you route raw notes via our API (hosted) with prefix/KV caching, or will the workload be a batch of files uploaded to a customer VPC?

Proposed PoC plan (we can adjust):
- Week 0: Sign PoC charter and NDA / procurement touchpoints (we can provide an MSA + SLA draft).
- Weeks 1–2: Hosted API spike to validate model behavior and functional success criteria (fastest onboarding; no infra changes).
- Weeks 3–6: If Hosted validates functionality but security requires isolation, move to Dedicated reserved capacity for load and latency validation; parallel private-dry-run (network readiness checks) so VPC setup can finish.
- Success criteria (example):
  - Functional: >95% extraction accuracy on your test set (existing eval harness).
  - Latency/cost: P95 < 200ms for interactive flows; cost per 1k requests estimate within provided budget envelope.
  - Operational: KV cache hit rate >30% on repeat prefixes; end-to-end audit logs with customer KMS key recorded.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ve attached a one-page PoC charter template — if you can drop in the stakeholders, budget constraints, and target metrics we’ll convert to a signed PoC.
- Please confirm whether Procurement will insist on Dedicated for the trial or if running Hosted initially is acceptable to speed things up.
- If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min technical dry-run with Ben (SE) next week to capture sample payloads and token length distributions.

Attachments: PoC_Charter_Template.pdf, SLA_Draft_2026-10.docx

Thanks — looking forward to aligning the trial.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.inference

From: Ethan Clarke <ethan.clarke@medstream.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medstream.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mode qualification and PoC charter — MedStream follow-up

Jonas — thanks for the recap and the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Long-term we will need Private VPC (PHI + internal compliance). For a PoC, procurement will prefer Dedicated if it reduces legal overhead, but security wants to run a Private VPC assessment in parallel. So your outlined approach (Hosted spike -> Dedicated -> Private dry-run) sounds sensible.

2) Performance goals: P95 < 180ms is our goal for the interactive path, but we can accept 200ms as an upper bound during the early Dedicated test. Peak concurrency: 100–150 concurrent real-time streams; batch end-of-day peak of ~20k requests over 30 minutes.

3) Data flow: For the Hosted spike we can provide sanitized sample payloads; for Dedicated and Private we will route encrypted payloads over your VPC peering.

Stakeholders (for the charter):
- Ethan Clarke (Product/ML) — ethan.clarke@medstream.ai
- Priya Ramesh (Security lead) — priya.ramesh@medstream.ai
- Procurement team — procurement@medstream.ai
- Vikram Shah (Ops) — vikram.shah@medstream.ai

Procurement has asked for an initial cost and SLA estimate up front. Can you provide a short cost ballpark for the 2-week Hosted spike and an example Dedicated reservation size for ~150 concurrent streams? Also — can you attach SOC2 evidence or a link to your compliance page so Procurement has something to review?

Ethan
Ethan Clarke
Head of Product, MedStream AI
ethan.clarke@medstream.ai
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>

Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mode qualification and PoC charter — MedStream follow-up

Ethan — thanks, this helps. A few technical notes and a concrete trial proposal based on your numbers: 

Quick technical clarifications we need for sizing:
- Typical prompt + response token estimate per request (avg): please share an approximate mean and 95th percentile token size for both interactive and batch flows.
- KV caching: do you expect repeated prefixes across streams (e.g., templated discharge text)? If yes, caching will materially reduce cost and improve P95.

Proposed trial (detailed):
A) Hosted spike (2 weeks) — goal: functional parity and early accuracy checks
- We provision a hosted endpoint with streaming enabled and attach your sanitized test set. SE work: capture token distributions and create an eval run.
- Deliverables: accuracy report, token-latency profile, estimate of per-1k cost on hosted model.

B) Dedicated sizing window (2–4 weeks) — goal: scale and latency validation
- Based on token profiles we’ll recommend a Dedicated pool size (GPU type / instance count). For your ~150 concurrent interactive streams we anticipate recommending between 4–8 A100-equivalent GPUs depending on sequence lengths and KV cache hit rates. We’ll provide two sizing buckets (conservative / optimized).
- Deliverables: load test report, P95 numbers, recommended reservation size and cost estimate.

C) Private dry-run (parallel) — ops & network readiness
- While Dedicated tests run, we’ll start VPC peering and run smoke tests to validate KMS integration / audit logs. If peering completes earlier, we can cut over to a Private VPC test.

Attachments: I filled the attached PoC charter with the stakeholders you listed and a draft scope (PoC_Charter_MedStream_filled.pdf). I also attached a short SLA draft for Procurement to review.

Next actions:
- Ethan: confirm token-size estimates or share a representative sample payload by EOD Wed so Ben and I can size properly.
- Procurement: if you want a ballpark cost now, we can provide: Hosted 2-week spike ~ $6k–$12k (depends on model size); Dedicated 4-week validation with 4–8 GPU reservation estimate ~ $18k–$48k (includes support hours). We'll refine after we see token profiles.

If helpful, Ben can run a 30-min deep-dive on Wednesday to capture payload examples and walk through caching expectations.

— Monica
